0.long_answer: Distal renal tubular acidosis (type I RTA) is primarily a disorder of the kidney’s ability to acidify the urine due to the failure of the alpha-intercalated cells. These cells are located in the distal tubule and cortical collecting duct and are responsible for secreting hydrogen ions into the urine. When these cells fail to function properly, acid secretion is impaired, leading to the accumulation of acid in the body, manifesting as metabolic acidosis.
